meaning: to invade, to raid, to trespass
headline: Okasu, “to invade”, is a doublet of 犯す (okasu, “to commit (crime)”) and 冒す (okasu, “to risk”).

sources.quote: Doublet of 犯す (okasu, “to commit (crime)”) and 冒す (okasu, “to risk”).

pos: nouns which may take the genitive case particle 'no'
headline: アラブ is an internationalism, ultimately from Arabic, first cited in Japanese in a 1914 dictionary of loanwords.

sources.quote: Internationalism, ultimately from Arabic عَرَب (ʕarab); see English Arab.
First cited in Japanese to a dictionary of loanwords from 1914.

headline: Satsujin is 殺 (satsu, “killing”) plus 人 (jin, “human”).

sources.quote: Compound of 殺(さつ) (satsu, “killing”) + 人(じん) (jin, “human”).

headline: Maneki is the continuative stem of the verb 招く (maneku, “to invite, call over”).

sources.quote: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 招(まね)く (maneku, “to invite, call over”).

headline: Zai, “fortune”, is from Middle Chinese 財 (MC dzoj).

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 財 (MC dzoj).

headline: Susugu was originally pronounced unvoiced, as 濯く (susuku).

sources.quote: Originally pronounced unvoiced, as 濯(すす)く (susuku).

pos: noun or participle which takes the aux. verb suru
headline: Shūshū is from Middle Chinese 收集, first appearing around 760 CE with the spelling 聚集 in kanbun texts.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 收集 (MC syuw dzip, “to collect, to gather”), from 收 (MC syuw, “to receive, to collect”) + 集 (MC dzip, “to gather”). First appears in roughly 760 CE with the spelling 聚集 in kanbun texts.
The 収集 spelling appears to be more common in modern usage.

meaning: to face on, to look out on to
headline: Men suru is 面 (men, “face”) plus する (-suru).

sources.quote: 面(めん) (men, “face”) + する (-suru)

headline: Azawarau is 嘲 (aza, “something off-color or not quite right”) plus 笑う (warau, “laugh”).

morphemes.meaning: something off-color or not quite right

sources.quote: Compound of 嘲 (aza, “something off-color or not quite right”, compounding element found in terms such as 嘲る (azakeru, “to ridicule, to jeer at”) and 欺く (azamuku, “to deceive”), cognate with 痣 (aza, “bruise”)) + 笑う (warau, “laugh”).

headline: Hachimitsu is 蜂 (hachi, “bee”) plus 蜜 (mitsu, “honey”).

sources.quote: Compound of 蜂(はち) (hachi, “bee”) + 蜜(みつ) (mitsu, “honey”).

headline: インテリ is from the Russian word intelligéncija.

sources.quote: From Russian интеллиге́нция (intelligéncija).

headline: Torimodosu is 取る (toru, “to take”) plus 戻す (modosu, “to return, put back”).

sources.quote: 取(と)る (toru, “to take”) + 戻(もど)す (modosu, “to return, put back”)

headline: Kinjiru is a shift from the verb 禁ずる (kinzuru), as -uru verbs moved to the -iru pattern.

sources.quote: Shift from verb 禁(きん)ずる (kinzuru), by natural progression from サ行変格活用 (sa-gyō henkaku katsuyō, “s-irregular conjugation”) verbs ending in -uru to 上一段活用 (kami ichidan katsuyō, “upper monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -iru.

pos: noun or participle which takes the aux. verb suru
headline: Shōdaku is 承 (shō, “agree to”) plus 諾 (daku, “consent”).

sources.quote: From 承 (shō, “agree to”) + 諾 (daku, “consent”).

headline: Shotchū is possibly from 初中後 (shochūgo).

sources.quote: Possibly from 初中後 (shochūgo).

headline: Yashiki is 屋 (ya, “house”) plus 敷 (shiki, “building site”), short for 敷地 (shikichi).

sources.quote: From 屋(や) (ya, “house”) + 敷(しき) (shiki, “building site”, short for 敷(しき)地(ち) (shikichi)).

headline: Kasen is 河 (ka, “river, large river”) plus 川 (sen, “river”).

sources.quote: From 河 (ka, “river, large river”) + 川 (sen, “river”).

meaning: to exhaust, to run out; to devote, to serve
headline: Tsukusu is from Old Japanese, found in the Man'yōshū and spelled phonetically as 都久須.

sources.quote: From Old Japanese [script needed] (tukusu). Found in the Man'yōshū, completed some time after 759 CE, spelled phonetically in man'yōgana as 都久須.

term: デモンストレーション
kana: デモンストレーション
headline: デモンストレーション is from English demonstration.

morphemes.text: デモンストレーション
morphemes.reading: デモンストレーション

sources.quote: From English demonstration.

headline: ショー is borrowed from English show.

sources.quote: Borrowed from English show.

headline: Wataridori is 渡り (watari, the stem of 渡る (wataru, “to migrate”)) plus 鳥 (tori, “bird”).

sources.quote: From 渡(わた)り (watari, 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 渡(わた)る (wataru, “to migrate”)) + 鳥(とり) (tori, “bird”).

headline: Kokoromiru is 心 (kokoro, “heart, mind”) plus 見る (miru, “to look, watch, take care”).

sources.quote: From 心 (kokoro, “heart, mind”) + 見る (miru, “to look, watch, take care”).
The み (mi) is written as an okurigana to indicate the reading of 試.

headline: Zadankai is, by surface analysis, 座談 (zadan) plus 会 (-kai).

sources.quote: By surface analysis, 座談(ざだん) (zadan) + 会(かい) (-kai).

headline: Atsuryoku is 圧 (atsu, “pressure”) plus 力 (-ryoku, “power”).

sources.quote: 圧(あつ) (atsu, “pressure”) + 力(りょく) (-ryoku, “power”)

meaning: (arch) dojo, hall used for martial arts training, mandala
headline: Dōjō is from Middle Chinese 道場, literally “way + place”, itself originally a translation of a Sanskrit term for “seat of wisdom”.

sources.quote: /daudiau/ → /dɔːd͡ʑɔː/ → /doːʑoː/
From Middle Chinese 道場 (MC dawX drjang, literally “way + place”), itself originally a translation of Sanskrit बोधिमण्ड (bodhimaṇḍa, “seat of wisdom”).

headline: ベストセラー is from English bestseller.

sources.quote: From English bestseller.

headline: Kanten is 観 (kan, “to view”) plus 点 (ten, “point”).

sources.quote: From 観 (kan, “to view”) + 点 (ten, “point”).

headline: Nae is from Old Japanese and is an apophonic form of 苗 (nawa, “seedling”).

sources.quote: From Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *napay.
Apophonic form of 苗(なわ) (nawa, “seedling”, bound form, only used in compounds), similar to nouns such as 神 (kami, kan-, kamu-, “god”) and 目 (me, ma-, “eye”).

meaning: to mix, to converse with, to cross (swords)
headline: Majieru is from Old Japanese 交ふ (mazifu), a lower bigrade verb.

sources.quote: From Old Japanese 交ふ (mazifu), in the 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) pattern.
Development

Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.

meaning: naturally, as a matter of course
headline: Onozukara was originally 己 (ono, “oneself”) plus つ (tsu, possessive particle) plus 柄 (kara, “quality, characteristic”).

sources.quote: Originally a compound of 己 (ono, “oneself”) + つ (tsu, possessive particle) + 柄 (kara, “quality, characteristic”, later developing senses of “from, because”).

meaning: one's father, old man, one's boss
headline: Oyaji is perhaps 親 (oya, “parent”) plus 父 (chichi, “father”), altered from an earlier form, oyachichi.

sources.quote: Perhaps from 親 (oya, “parent”) + 父 (chichi, “father”). The reading appears to be an alteration of an earlier form, oyachichi, perhaps under the influence of 爺 (chichi, jiji, jī, “old man”). The kanji are jukujikun (熟(じゅく)字(じ)訓(くん)).
